title: Sedmica 1 — ponavljanje
theme: Week 1 review + postcards from across BiH
reviewerNotes: Revised Week 1 review to open BiH geography (Jajce, Blagaj, Počitelj) instead of recycling Sarajevo-only imagery — ready for human review.
storyBeat: Ana captions her Sarajevo week — then Emir slides in postcards from Jajce, Blagaj, and Počitelj so the review opens the whole country.

vocabulary: Recycle Week 1: greetings, biti, numbers/café, family, places, time
Light diary words: sedmica, foto, priča
grammar: Remember: Gdje je…? and Koliko je sati?
culture: Week 1 photo captions as memory tools
New places beyond the big two: Jajce, Blagaj (Buna), Počitelj

grammar.title: Remember — biti and possessives
grammar.explanation: Week 1 core: Ja sam Ana. Ti si Emir. On je / Ona je… Pair with possessives: Moj prijatelj. Moja prijateljica. Moja mačka. If a noun ends in -a, try moja first.

examples.bosnian: Ja sam Ana. Ti si Emir.
examples.english: I am Ana. You are Emir.

grammar.title: Remember — where and when
grammar.explanation: Place kit: Gdje je…? Ovdje. Tamo. U Sarajevu. Kod Amire. Time kit: Koliko je sati? Danas / sutra + weekday. Put them in one diary line: Danas sam kod Amire. Sutra — mapa!

examples.bosnian: Koliko je sati? — Deset je sati.
examples.english: What time is it? — It is ten.

culture.title: Diary of a week — and postcards farther out
culture.body: Ana can caption Sebilj and kahva now. Emir will not let Week 1 end as a two-city postcard rack. He adds three images from across Bosnia and Herzegovina: the Pliva waterfall at Jajce, where a river falls through the town; the Blagaj tekija tucked under a cliff at the Buna spring; and Počitelj’s stone houses stacked above the Neretva valley. Review the language — then aim your next sutra at a wider map. Book 1 lives in Sarajevo for the plot, but the country is the classroom.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson A — Recycle the toolkit
lessonBlocks.body: Rapid fire without notes: Zdravo! Ja sam… Drago mi je. Kahvu, molim. Koliko? Moj brat / Moja sestra. Gdje je mapa? Ovdje / tamo. Koliko je sati? Danas / sutra. Emir times Ana for two minutes. Misses are fine — laugh, repeat, move on. Circle three weak words and write them once with accents.
tips: Speed over perfection — then one careful rewrite
Revisit čćšžđ from Lesson 1 if typing slips

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson B — Photo diary captions
lessonBlocks.body: Caption six lines for Week 1 skills — then three bonus place lines Emir teaches as teases: Jajce — vodopad. Blagaj — Buna. Počitelj — stari grad. You do not need full sentences yet; glue them with Gdje je…? and Tamo. Share the diary at the table; Amira stamps the week with Hvala — i sutra! Week 2 will feed you burek and more of the map.
tips: Week 1 lines first; then three new place names
Reuse Gdje je…? / Tamo for the postcard stack

funFacts.title: Jajce — town on a waterfall
funFacts.body: In Jajce the Pliva River drops as a waterfall right by the old town — a rare urban cascade and a medieval royal seat of the Bosnian kingdom.

funFacts.title: Blagaj and the Buna spring
funFacts.body: At Blagaj, a Dervish tekija (tekke) sits under a cliff where the Buna River bursts from the rock — one of the strongest karst springs in the region.

funFacts.title: Počitelj’s stone stack
funFacts.body: Počitelj climbs a hillside in Herzegovina in stone houses and a fortress silhouette — a preserved Ottoman-era settlement above the Neretva corridor.

funFacts.title: Banja Luka next on the mental map
funFacts.body: Farther north, Banja Luka spreads along the Vrbas with the Kastel fortress. Week reviews should keep adding real towns so BiH never shrinks to two postcard cities.
